abstract: Maintains coastal lifeboat cutter patrol dispositions and ocean surface wave state observations
system_message:
You are Maritime Rescue Coordinator (MAR). The Maritime Rescue Coordinator (MAR) monitors coastal lifeboat cutter patrol dispositions and ocean surface wave state observations along active maritime evacuation transit lanes and open water channel sections.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: trailing 6-hour observation window·Maintains coastal lifeboat cutter patrol dispositions and ocean surface wave state observations（SURV）
information_points.content:
MAR-SURV-8II：For the Sound of Barra Trans-Island Vector across the trailing 6-hour observation window, the sea rescue vessel escort is ready with an active patrol cutter escort, and the maximum wave crest height along open water channel sections is 3 m.
MAR-SURV-5F4：For the Hebridean Coastal Relief Channel across the trailing 6-hour observation window, the sea rescue vessel escort is not ready, and the maximum wave crest height along open water channel sections is 2 m.
MAR-SURV-81O：For the Minch Northern Deep-Water Flightway across the trailing 6-hour observation window, the sea rescue vessel escort is not ready, and the maximum wave crest height along open water channel sections is 2 m.

information_points.title: trailing 1-hour observation window·Maintains coastal lifeboat cutter patrol dispositions and ocean surface wave state observations（COASTREC）
information_points.content:
MAR-COASTREC-T7J：For the Hebridean Coastal Relief Channel during the trailing 1-hour observation window, the sea rescue vessel escort is not ready, while the maximum wave crest height along open water channel sections is 2 m.
MAR-COASTREC-T2C：For the Minch Northern Deep-Water Flightway during the trailing 1-hour observation window, the sea rescue vessel escort is ready with an all-weather emergency cutter escort stationed on active patrol, and the maximum wave crest height along open water channel sections is 4 m.
MAR-COASTREC-HVJ：For the Sound of Barra Trans-Island Vector during the trailing 1-hour observation window, the sea rescue vessel escort is ready with an all-weather emergency cutter escort on active patrol, and the maximum wave crest height along open water channel sections is 3 m.
